entries.grounds: Original guard `home != '/nonexistent'` (confine.py:570), mutant `home != ''`. `home` is never '' (the only producer, _probe confine.py:365 `env.get('HOME') or '/nonexistent'`; the only caller of _judge is :422), so the mutant always applies the HOME listing check, while the original skips it exactly when home is the placeholder string (an absent or empty HOME, or a literal HOME=/nonexistent). For every other home both guards are True and the programs agree. For home == '/nonexistent' they disagree, but the outcomes still agree unless `ls -A /nonexistent` inside lists an entry that no mount below it names (names, :567-568, excludes at == home). The probe lists $5 only `if [ -e "$5" ]` (PROBE confine.py:71), and /nonexistent exists inside only (a) as the parent bubblewrap makes for a mount below it, where every listed entry is that mount's own first path component (shown <= names in both programs), or (b) as a bind of a HOST directory /nonexistent that has content. (b) needs that directory on the host AND bound by wrap: an operator read_only entry (wrap :185-187 refuses a missing one), the client's directory (:188), the workspace, a bare common git directory (:196); the config directory ends in 'opencode' and every other mount is a fixed path (argv :166-174). Nothing the wrapper builds creates /nonexistent. In state (b) the original admits and the mutant refuses ('HOME shows more than...') although no HOME is set: a false refusal, fail-closed; neither program admits a breach. Not re-measured in a Linux guest (none here): bubblewrap's creation of the parent directory is the earlier audit's measurement and its documented behaviour.

entries.grounds: `_survivors('120.NNNNNN')` instead of `_survivors('sleep 120.NNNNNN')` (confine.py:380; _survivors :430-441): `command in pr.command` is a substring test, so every command line holding the original's 'sleep 120.N' holds '120.N' (the mutant's match set contains the original's: no under-reporting). Extra matches can only be a process whose command line carries the probe's nonce-derived number without 'sleep ' before it: the probe's own descendants (bwrap's argv, the pid-1 helper, `sh -c PROBE probe ... $7`). When _survivors is called subprocess.run has returned, i.e. the outer bwrap has been reaped and the probe shell has exited; a helper the kernel is still tearing down is looked at again for SURVIVOR_GRACE (:92, :436-441). Whatever remains is a process the session left, and a survivor is only ever a claim (cleanup_authority.signal_owned proves ownership before any signal, cleanup_authority.py:372-404). entries.grounds: `sorted(spec) != list(KEYS)` and `sorted(spec) != sorted(KEYS)` (confine.py:122) are the same predicate: KEYS (:46) is a module-level tuple literal written in sorted order ('backend' < 'bwrap' < 'network' < 'read_only') and is never rebound (`KEYS =` appears once in confine.py; no patch.object(confine, 'KEYS') anywhere), so sorted(KEYS) == list(KEYS) for every run of the program.

entries.grounds: The mutant drops the literal closing brace of 'confinement is {backend, bwrap, network, read_only}' (confine.py:123). The text is the SettingsError reason an operator reads (cli.py:92-94 prints it after 'aisef run: refused:') or the verifier prints in a problem line (verify.py:58-63 "the record's settings do not load: {e}"); both interpolate it with an f-string, nothing parses it, matches its closing bracket or uses it as a format template, and nothing follows it that it could fuse with (it is raised on its own: run.py:405 joins measure()'s problems, never problem()'s). The tests that touch it match 'confinement is' (test_v21_confine.py:326) or each key as a word (T07b.py:126-129, words() ignores punctuation).

entries.grounds: The earlier grounds hold as to behaviour: the mutant moves XDG_DATA_HOME from /aisef-home/.local/share to the sandbox HOME itself, the per-session `--tmpfs /aisef-home` (confine.py:171), so what the client writes still lands in the namespace's own tmpfs and dies with it; the other two XDG variables keep distinct subdirectories (:198-199); nothing in the probe reads XDG_* (PROBE uses $1..$9). What no longer holds is 'nothing reads a value back / no test separates it': since round 3 the environment wrap returns is handed, value for value, to the probe's subprocess (_probe :349, :373) and a requirement test pins it exactly. The test the earlier grounds cite (test_v21_confine.py, test_home_is_an_empty_tmpfs_...:395-400) only asserts `startswith(confine.HOME)` (:399), which the mutant satisfies (its value IS confine.HOME).

entries.refutation: Input: confine.measure(spec, where, exe, environ={'PATH','HOME','XDG_CONFIG_HOME'}, system='linux') with subprocess.run recorded. Run at the snapshot with the mutant applied it FAILS (XDG_DATA_HOME='/aisef-home' instead of the expected value); on the unmutated copy all 10 tests of the file pass. Test owed: none to write; register tests/v2/test_v21_r3_conf_locale.py for 'aisef2/app/confine.py::wrap' (V21_TARGETS via _V21_R3_APPEND in validation/v2/mutation.py) and re-run the wrap mutants. Optional tightening of test_v21_confine.py:399 to `startswith(confine.HOME + '/')` and the three exact values.
